newsitem.title: UK: Provident Fin hit, talk of govt crack-down.
newsitem.headline: Provident Fin hit, talk of govt crack-down.

text.p: Shares in credit and insurance group Provident Financial Plc fell on Friday following a press report which said the government was planning to review companies that specialise in lending to the poor.
Shares in the company fell 22-1/2p or 3.5 percent to 612-1/2p by 0734 GMT. Cattles Plc also fell on the news to be down 15p or 4.4 percent at 323-1/2p.

The Times newspaper quoted Nigel Griffiths, Minister for Consumer Affairs, saying "We take a dim view of people on low incomes being exploited by lenders," and added that such companies were under review.
The newspaper said Provident Financial could be one of the companies on the government's "hit-list".
"The reason for the weakness in the shares are the comments in the press," said one dealer.
London Scottish Bank also lost 2p to be trading at 101-1/2p.
Provident Financial makes most of its profits from small cash loans to those deemed uncreditworthy by Britain's main banks.

Pre-tax profits for the last full-year period were up 17 percent and on Monday this week, the company said it intended to use some of its excess cash to buy-back up to 17 million shares over the next year.

Back in April, chief executive Howard Bell told Reuters he was confident that an incoming Labour government would not pose a threat to Provident's high interest lending. The newspaper said Provident charges a flat rate of 59 percent, equivalent to 164 percent APR.

Cattles saw profits growth of 20 percent in 1996. The group's main business remains door-to-door moneylending but in 1996 the percentage of Cattles profits which came from its home collected credit business fell to 65 percent from 90 percent in 1994.
Traders speculated that Manchester-based London Scottish Bank, another publicly quoted moneylender was another potential target for the government.
